summary: A short query asking whether any ARPANET host offered an interpreter for MIX, Knuth's hypothetical computer, and an assembler for its language MIXAL, for students of The Art of Computer Programming. If not, the author asked that some host provide one. RFC 494 and RFC 485 follow on.

plainLanguage.summary: This short RFC asks whether a network computer can run Knuth's hypothetical MIX machine and assemble MIXAL programs. It also asks whether a host would provide the tools if none were available.

subtitle: A question asking whether ARPANET hosts offered tools for Knuth's MIX computer.

tldr.problem: Students of The Art of Computer Programming wanted to run programs for Knuth's hypothetical MIX computer and its assembly language.
tldr.mechanism: D. Walden asks whether any Network host has a MIX interpreter and a MIXAL assembler, and asks whether a host would make them available if not.
tldr.outcome: RFC 473 is a request for information and records no answer in its own text.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 473 as Unknown, with no RFC recorded as updating or obsoleting it. It is a short resource request rather than a specification.

sections.title: The Question About MIX
sections.content: D. Walden asks whether an interpreter for MIX, Knuth's hypothetical computer, is available on any ARPA Network host. He asks about an assembler for MIXAL, the assembly language for MIX, as well.
sections.plainLanguage: MIX is a hypothetical computer described by Knuth. The author asks whether network hosts have software that can run its programs.

sections.title: The Intended Users
sections.content: The RFC says that the requested tools would serve students of The Art of Computer Programming. If no host already offered them, the author asked whether a Network host would make them available cheaply.
sections.plainLanguage: The request is aimed at people studying Knuth's book. They want a way to try the MIX examples using a network host.

sections.title: A Request, Not a Specification
sections.content: The note defines no protocol, software interface, or operating procedure. It asks the Network community whether the tools exist and whether a host might offer them.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC asks the community for a resource. It does not itself provide the MIX tools or say who answered.
